claim: Requirements gathering assumes needs already exist to be collected; elicitation is active discovery of unstated, tacit, and conflicting needs
quote: Requirements gathering is a passive collection of pre-existing artifacts and stated needs, while requirements elicitation is an active discovery process that uncovers unstated needs.

claim: The BA profession shifted from 'requirements gathering' to 'requirements elicitation' to reflect the active investigative role
quote: The BA profession has shifted from using the term 'requirements gathering' towards the preferred term 'requirements elicitation,' highlighting the active role that BAs play.

claim: BABOK v3 classifies elicitation techniques into three categories: Collaborative, Research, and Experimental
quote: There are three common types of elicitation activities: Collaborative, Research, and Experiments.

claim: Surveys work best as validation tools after other techniques have established baseline understanding, not as a primary first technique
quote: Distributing surveys as the primary elicitation technique early in a project produces surveys that will not produce useful answers.

claim: Optimal workshop size is 8-12 participants; larger groups reduce engagement; use lo-fi wireframes in prototyping; schedule observation during peak load
quote: Optimal workshop participation ranges from eight to twelve attendees for productive discussion. Larger groups reduce engagement and focus.

claim: Structured interviews are the most commonly used elicitation technique; preparation with agendas separates productive from meandering interviews
quote: This is by far the most common technique that business analysts use.

claim: The five-step elicitation process: plan, prepare, conduct, document, confirm; confirmation step circulates findings to stakeholders
quote: Circulate to stakeholders for review and refinement. Failure to define business needs clearly can lead to expensive mistakes or system failure.

claim: Combine 3-5 complementary techniques per project; plan iterative elicitation rounds since stakeholders rarely deliver complete requirements in a single session
quote: Business Analysis teams often rely only on one technique such as interviews for elicitation, but a Business Analyst should use a combination of complementary elicitation techniques.

claim: Job shadowing and contextual interviews reach tacit knowledge and undocumented workarounds that surveys cannot
quote: Tacit knowledge and undocumented workarounds need observation, with job shadowing and contextual interviews reaching what surveys cannot.

claim: Ambiguity in requirement statements indicates tacit knowledge that can cause critical complications in later development stages
quote: Ambiguity in requirement statements indicates the presence of tacit knowledge, which can act as a root cause of critical complications in later stages of software development.

claim: EventStorming maps to user stories: events become acceptance criteria, commands become story actions, policies become business rules
quote: From Event Storming to User Stories: events become acceptance criteria, commands become story actions.

claim: Attaching EventStorming board artifacts directly to LLM prompts produced 3x more domain concepts in a prototype than unstructured prose description
quote: Prototype v2 contained three times the domain concepts as v1 (9 schemas vs. 3), derived purely from richer collaborative artifacts—same LLM, better input.

claim: EventStorming and user story mapping serve different purposes and are complementary: EventStorming for domain discovery, story mapping for UX-centric feature planning
quote: Story mapping and event storming serve different purposes; they can be complementary, and using a combination can lead to a more comprehensive understanding.

claim: Open-source Claude BA skill automates stakeholder analysis, RACI matrices, and acceptance criteria drafting from rough notes
quote: The IT Business Analyst Skill for Claude transforms how Business Analysts produce deliverables, addressing the challenge that BAs spend extraordinary amounts of time on document assembly.

claim: Fireflies.ai auto-transcribes calls with speaker labels; Grain timestamps and clips key moments from user interviews; Whimsical AI converts requirement text into wireframes and user stories
quote: AI tools automate requirements gathering by recording stakeholder meetings, summarizing feedback, identifying missing elements, and generating drafts of documentation.

claim: aqua AI creates structured requirements from 15-second voice input and detects duplicates (~20% of typical backlogs); automatically generates test cases
quote: You speak for 15 seconds, and Aqua's AI creates a detailed and structured requirement that is ready for review. Reduces redundant tickets (approximately 20% of typical backlogs).

claim: Treat AI output as a junior analyst's first draft; Copilot4DevOps checks requirements quality against INCOSE standards within Azure DevOps
quote: Generative AI is best thought of as a requirements management assistant. Human review corrects AI errors and ensures alignment with organizational needs.

claim: State-of-practice study across 12 companies found interviews and workshops used universally; observation underused despite uniquely capturing tacit process knowledge
quote: The State-of-Practice in Requirements Elicitation: An Extended Interview Study at 12 Companies.

claim: Requirements defects discovered at UAT cost many times more to fix than defects caught in elicitation; poor elicitation consequences appear weeks or months later
quote: Consequences of poor elicitation appear weeks or months later when a developer builds something that does not match what the business intended; by the time these consequences become visible, the cost of addressing them is many times higher.

claim: ChatGPT and Claude can generate structured interview guides and BRD drafts from domain briefs, with PMs reporting 67% of documentation time saved
quote: Creating a comprehensive BRD from scratch can consume 8-12 hours of focused work, with 67% of Product Managers reporting that documentation takes up more time than stakeholder meetings.
